text:
kevin-cs: Hey team, KitePay is seeing a flood of 429s in prod starting ~02:00 UTC. They say no deploys. Most responses include X-RateLimit headers showing the minute bucket exhausted. Happening across several worker hosts, not just one. Can we triage?

maria: Thanks — can you paste a raw request/headers and the X-RateLimit values? Also need their API key id and whether these are streaming sessions or short requests.

kevin-cs: Here's the header dump they provided (redacted):

  Authorization: Bearer sk_live_REDACTED
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-Client-App: kitepay-syncer

Response headers on 429: 
  X-RateLimit-Limit-Minute: 1800
  X-RateLimit-Remaining-Minute: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset-Minute: 14
  Retry-After: 60

They say ~400 TPM and occasional spikes to 2500 TPM for short bursts.

alex: Quick thought — if they have many long-lived streaming connections or token-refresh retries that all retry simultaneously, that can pile into the minute window. Do we have per-key RPM/TPM graphs for api_key=kitepay-prod?

julia: I pulled metrics for that key: minute-rate peaked at 3k for two 10s windows at 02:05 and 02:15, then dropped. Average across the hour still <600/min. Looks like short bursts hitting the minute cap.

maria: Do their client logs show retry loops? Common pattern: non-jittered backoff + credential refresh scheduled at exact minute boundary. Ask if they refresh tokens every 60s.

kevin-cs: They confirmed a background worker that refreshes tokens every 60s and immediately replays queued jobs. No jitter.

alex: That explains it. If N workers refresh at same second, you get a mini stampede that fills the minute bucket. Recommended mitigations: add jitter to refresh, limit concurrent outbound streams per host, and exponential backoff on 429 with full jitter.

maria: Immediate mitigations we suggested to customer: reduce concurrent streams from 25 -> 5, add random jitter +/- 30s to refresh schedule, and cap retries to 3 with exponential backoff (base 500ms).

kevin-cs: They implemented the jitter + reduced concurrency. Restarted workers. Early telemetry shows minute peaks down to ~700/min and no 429s in the last 5m. :thumbsup:

julia: For follow-up, recommend they move bursty syncs to a queued worker that rate-limits client-side to X req/min per API key, or apply a rolling window in their scheduler so refreshes don't align to wall-clock minute.

alex: For our side, we should add a dashboard annotation for "token-refresh stampede" pattern: high TPM spikes aligned to 00s in each minute and synchronous retry indicators. Query idea: group_by floor(ts/60) and count requests per key and host.

maria: Also told them about the Dedicated option for predictable throughput and higher minute windows, plus our quick guide on client-side exponential backoff.

kevin-cs: Customer asked if we can temporarily bump minute quota while they roll out changes. Can we do a short, manual quota increase for this key?

alex: We can do a temporary raise for 30m from the console. @maria can you approve?

maria: Approved to increase from 1800->3600 for 30 minutes. Please document in ticket and revert after.

srebot: [alert] quota-change executed by maria: api_key=kitepay-prod, old_minute=1800, new_minute=3600, duration=30m

kevin-cs: Thanks — after bump + client fixes they report no 429s for 40m. We'll follow up if anything recurs.

julia: Logging notes for postmortem: cause = synchronized token refresh + no jitter; mitigations = client jitter, concurrency cap, temporary quota bump, guidance docs.

alex: Adding a short blurb to support KB: "429 from client-side refresh storms" with sample code for jitter/backoff. Example client pseudocode we recommended:

  // refresh scheduler with jitter\  const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 30000) - 15000; // +/-15s\  setInterval(() => { setTimeout(refreshTokens, jitter); }, 60000);

  // retry with full jitter\  async function retry(fn, tries=3) {
    for (let i=0;i<tries;i++) {
      try { return await fn(); } catch (e) {
        const delay = Math.random() * Math.pow(2, i) * 500; // ms
        await sleep(delay);
      }
    }
    throw new Error('max retries');
  }

maria: Good. I'm closing the active escalation but leaving ticket open for 48h to monitor. :white_check_mark:

kevin-cs: Appreciated — will ping if it resurfaces.

julia: Post-incident action: add an automated detector that flags keys with >3x median TPM in any 10s window and with RPS spikes aligned to the same second across hosts.

alex: Agreed. I'll draft the rule and share in #eng-sre for review.

srebot: [note] thread archived by system after 45m of inactivity
